configs.description: Chassis only - what you spec before deciding what goes in it. The 2 slot bays are EMPTY; cooling, psus are populated. Enough to power on and reach the box, which is the question most people ask first and the one `default` used to answer with whatever the drawing happened to be populated with.

gaps.wanted: the fixed MX80 faceplate (Figure 8, built-in 48x1GbE) - a different front panel that would be a second device or configuration; only the modular chassis is modelled.
the DC supply face (guide Figure 16 is isometric line art).
the weight and power tables - outside this extraction's text layer; L27/L29 warnings stand on the modules.
confirmation whether the rear CLK/SYNC jacks are SMB or BNC - drawn SMB, photo resolution insufficient.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

which optics actually run in each pluggable cage - as prose in `attrs.optics-<media>` for now, which at least reaches the group, and structurally once enough vendors are in to say what the vocabulary has to hold

a top-level `profile:` naming the device class, so that `specified` has something to judge the attrs against - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml for the classes that exist, which unlocks `specified` and with it the About panel, and comparison against other devices
`physical-context` on 6 bays (front 5, rear 1) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays
the Nautobot exporter is not importable - unlocks NetBox / Nautobot device-type export

provenance.chassis: datasheet-table - the guide chassis description: 3.5 x 17.5 x 23.46 in (88.9 x 445 x 596 mm), 2RU. Ears NOT MODELLED by convention
provenance.color: photo - dark charcoal chassis, silver MICs, dark blue RE panel and fan door (Juniper's MX80-era styling)
provenance.front: photo - MIC row y 7-41.5 with slots at x 25.0 and 193.4 (the reference unit carries the 20x1GE SFP MIC and the 2x10GE XFP MIC); PS 0/PS 1 at x 14.7/86.2 in the lower band; the blue RE panel from 162.6 to 406 carrying CONSOLE over AUX (x 190), ETHERNET over USB (x 213), EXT CLK A over B (x 232), the SYS OK / RE lamps and ONLINE/OFFLINE button at its left, and the four fixed XFP cages at centres 261.6-349.7 with LINK lamps, silkscreened 0-3 over 0/MIC 0; the MX80 badge at 355; the fan-tray door at 407-445
provenance.lifecycle: announced - the whole MX5-MX80 family is EOL (guide banners and family tables); per-SKU dates on the Juniper milestones page
provenance.other-faces: near-blank by evidence - rail bands estimated; axis conventions per viewer3d.js as the siblings
provenance.power: NOT STATED at chassis level in the extraction; per-module rows were not captured either. The L27/L29 warnings stand as the record
provenance.rear: photo - a blank cover plate over the upper-left aperture labelled MPC 0 / MIC 1, the CLK and SYNC jacks at x 68/105 (y 75), the two-hole earthing plate and ESD at the right. The jacks are drawn as SMB (photograph resolution cannot distinguish SMB from BNC - recorded)
provenance.scale: photo - per-axis anchoring of the front photograph (body between the ear wings anchored to 445 mm; rows to 88.9). Positions are single-pass readings approximate to ~2 mm
provenance.shared-chassis: guide - the MX5, MX10, MX40 and MX80 are one chassis with different capacity licences and MIC entitlements (guide Figures 5-9); they are modelled as ONE device with the SKUs as configurations. The FIXED MX80 variant (Figure 8, 48x1GbE built in) is a different faceplate and is not modelled - see gaps
provenance.sources: MX5/MX10/MX40/MX80 Hardware Guide, and the image-library photographs mx80-front-high and mx80-rear-high (the mx5 set is the same base asset, recorded in the photo catalogue). No mechanical drawing was available
